question: What is the minimum age to be an eligible voter for Lok Sabha elections?
solution:
The correct answer is __**18 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Who can Vote in India:**

 
 
• All citizens, regardless of their race, color, or previous condition of subjugation have the right to vote under the Citizenship Act which grants them protection **under the 15th Amendment.**
 
• As per the Election Commission of India, citizens are eligible to become voters under the following conditions:
 
• **Every citizen who is 18 years old on the qualifying date (January 1 of the year in case) unless disqualified, is eligible to be enrolled. Hence, Option 2 is correct.**
 
• Enrollment only at an ordinary place of residence.
 
• Enrollment only at one place.
 
• Overseas Indian deemed to be ordinarily resident at the address given in passport.
 
• Service voters are deemed to be ordinarily resident at their home address.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• 61st Constitutional Amendment Act:

 
 
• This **act lowered the minimum age** for being eligible to **vote in the Indian Elections** from 21 years to 18 years.
 
• It was passed in 1988.
 
• It was passed during the government of Prime Minister Rajeev Gandhi.
 
• The bill received the presidential assent on 28th March 1989.
 
• The then-president R Venkataraman assented to the bill.
 
• This was done by amending Article 326 of the Constitution, which concerns elections to the Lok Sabha and the Assemblies.
